items.title: [apnews.com] European-Japanese BepiColombo enters Mercury orbit ahead of two-probe science mission
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

BepiColombo, a joint mission of the European Space Agency and Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, entered orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21, completing an eight-year journey and becoming the second mission to orbit the planet. The two orbiters remain attached; they are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10 and take up different polar orbits, with science operations due to begin in April 2027. The mission will use the European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, called Mio, to study Mercury from separate vantage points. Their instruments are designed to examine the planet’s surface and interior, its magnetic field and the thin gas envelope around it, including how the magnetic field interacts with the solar wind. Controllers in Germany confirmed the spacecraft’s capture several hours after a series of braking thruster firings, with the spacecraft about 152 million kilometers away. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival from December 2025. Its nominal science mission is planned to last one Earth year, with an extension through 2029.

items.title: [sootoday.com] Canadian study finds daily cannabis use exceeds daily drinking among adults under 50
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Daily cannabis use is more common than daily alcohol consumption among Canadian adults under 50, according to a study published Monday in the Canadian Medical Association Journal. Researchers analyzed responses from 99,920 adults in Statistics Canada’s 2023-24 Canadian Community Health Survey: 5.7% reported daily cannabis use, compared with 5.2% for alcohol and 8.5% for cigarettes. The researchers say daily cannabis use is associated with cannabis use disorder, while smoking cannabis poses risks to lung health. About 68% of daily cannabis users reported smoking cannabis, and 41% said they began daily use after legalization. The study relied on self-reported responses and did not distinguish medical from non-medical use.

items.title: [bbc.com] Brazil activates protective measures after about 20 isolated Awá approach
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

About 20 Indigenous Awá living in isolation approached the Guajajara village of Tawari on Monday, November 16, in Arariboia Indigenous Territory, in the Brazilian state of Maranhão; they received yams and returned to the forest. Members of the Guajajara community recorded the encounter, and the organization Survival International shared the footage. The National Foundation for Indigenous Peoples (Funai) and Indigenous health personnel are in the area. The government activated an emergency coordination mechanism to assess the situation and health risks. Authorities said they are still assessing the initial information and that this isolated approach does not mean the Awá have abandoned their isolation. The reason for the visit has not been confirmed; Survival International linked it to pressure from illegal loggers, hunters, and ranchers on the territory. Local residents voiced concern about the thinness of some children and older people. There is also concern about the risk of infections, given the group’s limited exposure to common pathogens.

items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission is due to enter orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21 after an eight-year journey of about 6 billion miles, becoming only the second mission to orbit the planet. Its two orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface, interior and magnetic environment, including its unusually large metal core, the origins of its magnetic field and ice in permanently shadowed craters. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival, and reaching Mercury requires careful braking against the Sun’s gravity. The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter will map the surface’s composition and study the interior; Japan’s orbiter will measure the magnetic field and the planet’s thin sodium exosphere. The spacecraft are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with science operations planned to begin in April 2027.

items.title: [healio.com] Trials find BMI falls with semaglutide in children, tirzepatide in teens
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Results reported Nov. 16 from two phase 3 trials showed substantial reductions in body mass index (BMI) with semaglutide in children aged 6 to 11 with obesity and tirzepatide in adolescents aged 12 to 17. After 68 weeks, children receiving semaglutide had a 13.5% BMI decrease, compared with a 2.7% increase among those receiving placebo; in the 72-week teen trial, tirzepatide produced a 19-percentage-point greater BMI reduction than placebo. Both studies also recorded improvements in cardiometabolic measures, while gastrointestinal side effects were common. In the semaglutide trial, BMI began rising during a seven-week washout after treatment stopped. Ania Jastreboff, a Yale obesity researcher, said results from 26 weeks off treatment are expected in the coming months.

items.title: [phys.org] Deep-sea robot finds deepest volcanic deposits near Challenger Deep
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

The remotely operated vehicle Jason/Medea has found what researchers describe as the deepest documented underwater pyroclastic deposits, on the Mariana Trench wall about 6,000 meters below sea level. The rocks provide evidence of volcanic flows in the trench’s western forearc, where geologists expected little volcanic activity because the mantle is generally not hot enough to melt. The findings were published Nov. 23 in Frontiers in Earth Science. The team’s observations support the idea that the Pacific Plate bends steeply as it sinks beneath the Mariana plate. That could help explain Challenger Deep’s depth and bring magma-generating processes closer to the trench. But researchers have not identified the eruption sites or established how eruptions could produce these deposits under immense water pressure. They say further sampling and radiometric dating are needed. Jason/Medea cannot reach the seafloor below 6,500 meters, while Challenger Deep extends to about 11,000 meters.

items.content_html:

Researcher Kushal Chakrabarti analyzed 247,694 instruction lifetimes and attributed the pattern to agents’ imperfect recall of why older instructions were added. The coding agent Claude Code is also being used for projects beyond conventional software development, including hobbyist-built apps and hardware prototypes. A separate review of the free coding agent Freebuff warns that it logs mouse and keyboard input and may use submitted information for advertising and AI training.

items.title: [gizmodo.com] AI-driven flaw discovery strains patching as outages hit US services
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

AI tools are rapidly uncovering software vulnerabilities and helping automate cyberattacks as outages disrupt U.S. email, flight operations, banking services and an internal National Security Agency communications network. Cybersecurity experts have linked some disruptions to rushed fixes for newly found flaws, but Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said the incidents were separate operational problems and officials had no indication of malicious activity or a coordinated attack. Hackers are also using AI to automate attacks. The FBI said hackers used the Artex AI framework in attacks worldwide, with some gaining privileged access in under three hours, while Palo Alto Networks linked another framework, Cairn, to 25 operations against at least 19 organizations. Researchers also used AI to find Java4Shell, a flaw in Java’s Base64 decoding library that could let an attacker execute commands on a vulnerable server. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency urged organizations to patch it. U.S. regulators sent inquiries to banks affected by outages, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency plans a deeper review of the incidents. Canonical, the company behind Ubuntu, is separately offering AI-generated fixes to Ubuntu Pro customers through an optional early-release channel before its engineers complete normal review and testing.

items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Indianola, Texas a coastal town that was once the second largest port in Texas next to at the time Galveston.In 1956 the port received a shipment of camels as part of the United States Camel Corps experiment to replace horses and mules as the primary work animal for southwestern America.

During the Civil War, it was occupied by the Union army, once in 1862, then again a year later. Part of that regiment later drowned moving from Indianola to Matagorda island.

The island was later hit twice again, this time by hurricanes, in 1876 and 1886. The second hurricane was accompanied by a major fire and also submerged most of the town, killing hundreds.

Now basically no sign of the town is left other than a few plaques (one being a marker of where the courthouse used to be). It is however valued as a great spot for fishing for local trout, redfish and flounder.

International nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries warned on Nov. 16 that attacks on Ukraine’s electricity infrastructure are increasing the risk of a nuclear accident this winter. Ukraine’s three operating nuclear plants have nine generating reactors and supply about 80% of the country’s electricity this winter. The plants also need a stable power supply to run cooling and other safety systems. The International Atomic Energy Agency said military activity disrupted the grid in the week before Nov. 14, forcing some units to reduce output. The Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant is not generating electricity but needs external power to cool its nuclear material. It has lost off-site power 27 times since the war began and has relied on one external line since late March. Per Strand, who heads two of the regulatory groups, warned that a nationwide blackout could affect all nine operating reactors simultaneously and urged European countries to coordinate emergency preparations if attacks continue. items.title: [theguardian.com] Ceasefire lets hundreds flee occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Hundreds of civilians evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky reached Ukrainian-held territory on Saturday, Oct. 31, after a local ceasefire allowed them to leave and aid to enter. U.S. First Lady Melania Trump mediated the pause, while Pope Leo XIV urged access for aid and evacuations. The ceasefire began Tuesday in the southern Kherson region and was scheduled to end Sunday evening. Residents travelled by bus through occupied Crimea to Russia, then flew to Belarus and crossed into Ukraine’s Chernihiv region, where relatives and aid workers met them. Some evacuees said food supplies had run out and they had survived on garden plants. The ceasefire also allowed roads to be cleared of mines and food and medicine to enter Oleshky. Ukraine and Russia have not disclosed how many people left. Melania Trump said the convoy could safely evacuate more than 750 people; an estimated 1,700 remained in Oleshky before the operation. Russia’s human rights commissioner said both sides had agreed to continue humanitarian missions. The truce was set to expire Sunday night.

Canada’s federal government will not appeal an Alberta Court of Appeal ruling that parts of the Impact Assessment Act exceed federal authority and says it will amend the law to address the ruling. items.title: [elpais.com] Leo XIV denounces racism against Afro-Peruvians and recalls slavery
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Pope Leo XIV denounced the discrimination that Afro-Peruvians continue to face on November 14 and recalled the slavery and humiliation suffered by their ancestors. He did so during a meeting in Zaña, a town in northern Peru recognized as a site commemorating slavery and African cultural heritage. Leo expressed his affection for the community and spoke about crime, extortion, and insecurity affecting families in the area. The pontiff, who was bishop of the Diocese of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023, closed in Zaña the Jubilee Year marking the 300th anniversary of the canonization of Saint Toribio de Mogrovejo. In May, in his first encyclical, he had apologized on behalf of the Church for the role previous pontiffs played in legitimizing slavery in the Americas and for failing to condemn it for centuries. At the meeting, Analí Montenegro Mendoza, representative of the Afro-Peruvian community in the diocese, called for a Church in which no one feels inferior because of their skin color, history, or culture. Peru is the final stop on Leo's South American tour, which includes Argentina and Uruguay; he is expected to remain in the country until Monday, November 16.

items.title: [middleeasteye.net] Iran says three tankers hit mines in or east of Strait of Hormuz
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Iran’s Revolutionary Guard and navy said Saturday that three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in or east of the Strait of Hormuz. The Guard said two vessels, including a supertanker, caught fire in the southern strait, while Iran’s regular navy separately reported a third tanker disabled in a prohibited area to the east. The claims have not been independently verified. Iran did not identify the ships or their flags, and the reports gave no casualty details. Tehran says the vessels were using unauthorized routes with their tracking systems switched off and warns shipping companies to coordinate passage with Iranian authorities. The United States says it has cleared the main shipping lanes of mines while imposing a naval blockade on Iranian ports and supporting tankers transiting the waterway. Fires and explosions at sea have been reported repeatedly in recent weeks. The UK Maritime Trade Operations monitoring agency had not reported the alleged mine blasts, though it recorded five incidents in the strait that week. Qatar and Pakistan are mediating diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran.

items.title: [cyberscoop.com] Europol-led operation seizes malware infrastructure, finds 6.4 million stolen credentials
items.content_html:
🔭 ✏️

Law enforcement agencies in nine countries, coordinated by Europol and Eurojust, disrupted infrastructure used by Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC, seizing 235 servers and 257 domains and identifying 6.4 million stolen credential records. German authorities said the records came from more than 40,000 victims. The malware services enabled credential theft, remote access and the delivery of ransomware; investigators also cleaned 681 websites compromised to spread Gootloader. Authorities plan to share victim data with notification services, including Have I Been Pwned. On Nov. 13, that service listed 179,745 email addresses linked to CastleRAT infections and 893,000 unique passwords observed more than 3 million times on infected computers. Police advised WordPress users to change credentials, enable multifactor authentication and patch vulnerabilities.
